article.headline: The Competitor List Is the Research: What Coherent's 10-K Reveals About the Next Wave of Photonics Winners
article.lede: For years, a quiet corner of public disclosure has done the work most investors outsource to expensive sell-side analysts: the competitor table buried deep in a large-cap's annual SEC filing. A single such list from Coherent Corp.'s 2022 10-K named, among others, a Canadian specialty-materials firm then trading below a dollar that has since risen more than thirty-fold.
article.body:
The technique is almost embarrassingly simple. Every publicly traded U.S. company must describe, in its annual Form 10-K, the competitive landscape it operates within. Large, diversified industrials — particularly those in advanced photonics like Coherent Corp. (formerly II-VI Incorporated) — span enough product lines that their competitor disclosures read less like boilerplate and more like a curated shortlist of the world's best niche suppliers. The insight is that these competitors are named not by analysts guessing at market structure but by the incumbent itself, whose sales force has lost deals to these companies and whose engineers know their technology intimately. It is one of the few places in public markets where the expert opinion is also the legally certified disclosure.

The case of 5N Plus (TSX: VNP) is the archetype the original post invokes. The Montreal-based producer of ultra-high-purity specialty semiconductors — compound wafers, epitaxial substrates, and space-grade solar cells through its German subsidiary AZUR SPACE — appeared in Coherent's compound-semiconductor competitor section while trading around C$0.92. The company's specialty is the tellurium, germanium, indium, and gallium compounds that sit at the upstream end of the photonics supply chain, materials so critical and so difficult to substitute that demand is largely inelastic. By 2024, record revenue of $289 million (up 19% year-over-year) and Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million set the stage for a further surge; by mid-2026 the share price had reached C$35–36, a gain of roughly thirty-eight times from that 2022 trough. The compound that drove it was not the stock price but the underlying business: space solar panels for satellite constellations, compound semiconductor substrates for power electronics, and a vertically integrated position in critical materials that no Western rival could easily replicate.

The methodology works for several structural reasons. First, competitor lists in 10-Ks name true rivals, not aspirational benchmarks — a company lists a competitor because that competitor is winning business today. Second, the companies named tend to be privately held or listed on foreign exchanges, meaning most U.S.-focused research shops have no coverage and no institutional incentive to generate it. Third, the cadence is annual and public, creating a free recurring screen for anyone patient enough to read. Fourth, and perhaps most important, the filing arrives before the revenue inflection rather than after: Coherent named these photonics suppliers in 2022 because they were already worthy of attention, not because they had already been re-rated.

The Coherent 10-K OCR'd in this post surfaces several names that warrant attention today. Eoptolink Technology (SZSE: 300502), the Chengdu-based optical transceiver maker, is no longer hidden — the company's 2025 net profit surged 236% year-over-year and its market capitalisation briefly exceeded 500 billion yuan before a single-quarter miss sent shares sliding 12% in April 2026. It has become, in effect, the Chinese hyperscaler-optics play, with InnoLight Technology an unlisted rival sharing roughly 60% of Nvidia's 800G SFP module orders between them. CASTECH (SZSE: 002222), founded in Fuzhou in 1990, grinds the nonlinear crystals — LBO, BBO, KTP — that seed almost every industrial and scientific laser; at roughly 92 yuan per share and a market cap of around 33 billion yuan, it is less flashy than a transceiver maker but arguably more defensible, having spent three decades building process know-how that is genuinely hard to copy. Accelink Technologies (SZSE: 002281) sits further up the photonics stack, combining transceiver modules, amplifiers, and passive optical components; its 2025 revenue run-rate approached 11.4 billion yuan, up 61% year-over-year, as AI-infrastructure spending in Chinese data centres translated directly into optical interconnect demand. Optowide Technologies (SSE: 688195), a smaller Fuzhou-based maker of molded aspheric lenses and fiber components with a market cap near 15 billion yuan, posted 31% revenue growth in 2024 with earnings up 67%; its thin analyst coverage — five firms at most — is precisely the information gap the 10-K-screening strategy is designed to exploit.

The SiC material competitors in the same Coherent filing point to a different but equally instructive narrative. Wolfspeed (NYSE: WOLF) — listed as a compound-semiconductor rival — filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2025 after accumulating $4.6 billion in debt while racing to build 200mm SiC fabs. It emerged ninety-one days later with debt reduced by 70%, but existing shareholders received only 3–5% of the reorganised entity's new equity. The lesson is not that 10-K competitor lists are infallible — they are not stock tips — but that the methodology surfaces the field and the investor's job is then to do the work: capital structure, competitive moat, management quality, and the timing of demand inflections. 5N Plus had a clean balance sheet and a quietly compounding substrate business; Wolfspeed had an audacious fab strategy and a debt load that assumed the CHIPS Act funding would arrive on schedule. Both were in the same Coherent filing. Reading the list is only the beginning.

The broader implication is that industrial incumbents with complex supply chains are, in effect, publishing maps of their own ecosystems once a year, for free. The investors who act on this are not insiders; they are diligent readers. In a market where most alpha is competed away by quantitative funds scanning the same financial databases, the 10-K competitor section remains one of the few sources of structured insight that requires only patience and a working knowledge of EDGAR — the SEC's full-text search system — to access. The names on Coherent's 2022 list that have already run — 5N Plus, Eoptolink — are now well-known. The names that have not yet run are the more interesting question.

concepts.definition: An annual report that U.S.-listed companies must file with the Securities and Exchange Commission, containing audited financial statements, business descriptions, risk factors, and competitive landscape disclosures.

An investment technique that uses the competitor tables in SEC 10-K filings to identify smaller, lesser-known rivals of well-covered large-cap companies — often listed on foreign exchanges with little institutional coverage — before they are re-rated by the market.

ticker_cohr.name: Coherent Corp.
ticker_cohr.blurb: Coherent Corp. (formerly II-VI Incorporated, rebranded after the 2022 acquisition of Lumentum rival Coherent) develops and manufactures engineered materials, optoelectronic components, and laser systems across three segments: Networking, Materials, and Lasers. Its Networking segment — the primary AI data-center play — supplies indium-phosphide chips, transceiver modules, and silicon-photonics sub-assemblies to hyperscalers and networking OEMs. With roughly $5.8 billion in fiscal 2025 revenue, it is one of the largest vertically integrated photonics companies in the world.
ticker_cohr.recent: Coherent joined the S&P 500 in March 2026, the same month it announced general availability of the industry's first dual-laser QSFP28-DCO module — a compact form factor enabling 100G coherent transmission over a single fiber with up to 300 km reach. At OFC 2026 the company showcased an expanded InP portfolio including 400 mW CW lasers, 200G/400G photodiodes, and 800G/1.6T modulators. Fifteen analysts hold an average "Strong Buy" rating with a consensus 12-month price target near $278.

ticker_lite.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
ticker_lite.blurb: Lumentum makes the lasers, optical chips, and components that go into the high-speed transceivers wiring AI data centres together. Spun out of JDSU in 2015, it spent its first decade as a 3D-sensing and telecom-optics supplier of moderate growth. The AI-cluster build-out has remade it into one of the principal upstream beneficiaries of hyperscaler capex, alongside Coherent Corp.
ticker_lite.recent: Q1 fiscal-2026 set record revenue, with management citing AI-driven demand and an order book that runs into 2027. In March 2026 Nvidia announced a roughly $2 billion strategic investment paired with multi-year purchase commitments for co-packaged-optics components. The company joined the S&P 500 in March 2026; shares have surged on AI demand, leaving the stock at a forward P/E in the 60s, materially above peers.

ticker_vnp.name: 5N Plus Inc.
ticker_vnp.blurb: 5N Plus Inc. (TSX: VNP) is a Montreal-based producer of ultra-high-purity specialty semiconductors and performance materials, operating in two segments. Specialty Semiconductors manufactures compound semiconductor wafers, epitaxial substrates, and advanced materials — principally from tellurium, germanium, indium, gallium, bismuth, and selenium — for applications in space solar cells, defence infrared sensors, and compound semiconductor devices. Performance Materials supplies bismuth and other high-purity metals for pharmaceutical, industrial, and energy applications. The company's German subsidiary, AZUR SPACE, is one of the world's leading manufacturers of space-grade multi-junction solar cells for satellite programmes, with production capacity expanded roughly 30% in 2025 and a further 25% expansion planned for the second half of 2026. 5N Plus appeared as a named competitor in Coherent Corp.'s 2022 10-K filing when shares traded near C$0.92; by mid-2026 the stock had reached C$35–36, a gain of roughly 38x.
ticker_vnp.recent: Full-year 2025 results featured 35% revenue growth and 73% higher Adjusted EBITDA, following record 2024 results (revenue up 19% to $289M, EBITDA up 39% to $53M). In February 2026 the company announced another 25% expansion of AZUR SPACE solar-cell capacity. The 52-week range as of May 2026 is C$5.12–C$36.40, with the stock having outperformed the TSX Composite by roughly 342 percentage points over the prior twelve months. The analyst consensus is Buy, with a target near C$37.65.

ticker_300502-sz.blurb: Eoptolink Technology Inc., Ltd. is a China-based company engaged in the research, development, manufacture, and sale of optical modules for optical communication applications. Its products include high-speed optical modules, silicon optical modules, coherent optical modules, and 800G LPO optical modules, serving markets such as 5G wireless networks, fixed broadband, data centers, and telecommunications. The company has a market capitalization of over 500 billion CNY and is a key player in the optical communication equipment sector.

The company reported strong financial results with revenue of 29.13B CNY and net income of 10.74B CNY, representing year-over-year growth of over 150%. The stock has gained more than 600% over the past year, driven by demand for high-speed optical modules in AI and data center applications.

ticker_wolf.name: Wolfspeed, Inc.
ticker_wolf.blurb: Wolfspeed designs and manufactures silicon carbide (SiC) power devices and substrates, positioning itself as the only vertically integrated producer at 200mm SiC wafer scale. Carved out of Cree in 2021, the company bet heavily on the EV and industrial power transition, sinking billions into the John Palmour Manufacturing Center in North Carolina and the Mohawk Valley Fab in New York. The ambition was sound; the balance sheet was not. After accumulating roughly $4.6 billion in debt and missing the expected CHIPS Act funding of $750 million, Wolfspeed filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on June 30, 2025. It emerged ninety-one days later in a prepackaged restructuring that eliminated ~70% of its debt, extended maturities to 2030, and cut annual cash interest expense by roughly 60%. Existing shareholders received only 3–5% of the reorganised equity; the bulk went to convertible noteholders (56.3%) and strategic investor Renesas (38.7%), who received new common stock plus warrants.
ticker_wolf.recent: Post-emergence, the reorganised Wolfspeed trades on NYSE under WOLF. The company's enterprise value at emergence was estimated at $2.35–2.85 billion (midpoint $2.6B), implying equity of $850M–$1.35B. As of May 2026 shares trade near $38. A December 2025 IRS settlement worth roughly $698 million provided unexpected cash relief. Chinese SiC substrate producers SICC (688234.SS) and TanKeBlue have gained market share during Wolfspeed's restructuring, while Infineon, STMicroelectronics, onsemi, and Rohm continue to invest in competing SiC capacity.

poster_aleabitoreddit.blurb: Serenity (@aleabitoreddit) is an X-based equity analyst whose feed concentrates on the AI hardware supply chain, with particular focus on what they call 'functional monopolies' — small or mid-cap suppliers occupying chokepoints in the photonics, advanced packaging and substrate value chains. Recurring names include Soitec ($SOI) for silicon-photonics substrates, Tower Semiconductor ($TSEM) for photonics foundry capacity, Coherent ($COHR) for transceivers, AXT ($AXTI) for indium phosphide, Lipoid Kosmetik / LPKF ($LPK) for glass-core substrates, and Japanese names such as TOWA (6315) and MSSCorp (6830) for HBM compression and CPO inspection respectively. The posting style mixes thesis posts with running performance updates and is frank about both wins and laggards.
poster_aleabitoreddit.recent: In early March 2026, ahead of NVIDIA's GTC, the account took what it described as a 'sizable position' in Soitec at roughly 43 EUR, framing the stock as a substrate-level monopoly on co-packaged optics that was trading at one times book. Subsequent posts charted the move higher (44%+ within five days, then 45.58%, then 'up 39.28% since last month' as it underperformed others in the photonics basket), and on May 4, 2026 the account marked the position up 'enormous amounts' alongside charts showing 517% YTD performance. The thesis tracks: the broader photonics rally has carried multiple names in their public list up triple digits over the same period.
poster_aleabitoreddit.credibility_note: Public posts show Serenity called Soitec at ~43 EUR in March 2026, before the rally documented in this bookmark, and has flagged related names (TSEM, AXTI, AAOI) ahead of large moves. Self-reported one-year returns of 630%+ should be treated as such — self-reported and unverified — but the timestamped Soitec call is a matter of public record.
